ササッとお弁当のフタで顔を隠す蒔寺。
どこから見てもチグハグな三人に挨拶をして、教室を後にする。
pages.en:
“Don't worry about it, Saegusa.

“And Makidera? I was the one who paid, and it was a crêpe, not taiyaki. Isn't it about time you broke that habit of rewriting history without even realizing it?”

“Gah. That smile really is terrifying.”

Makidera promptly ducks behind the lid of her lunchbox.

I say goodbye to the thoroughly mismatched trio and leave the classroom.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t worry, Saegusa-san.
And Makidera-san? I’m the one who paid, and it was crepes, not taiyaki. You should fix that habit of yours of changing the facts you remember, or I might have to reconsider things next time, okay?”
“Ugh. That smile is really scary.”
Makidera hides behind the lid of her lunch box.
Saying goodbye to the three of them, I leave the classroom.

pages.ja:
がらり、と教室のドアを閉める。
……と。
「ぶー。なんだよー、大差ないじゃんかタイヤキもクレープもー。どっちも甘いの皮で包んでるんだからさー」
蒔寺による女の子にあるまじき暴言が聞こえてきた。
pages.jaRuby:
がらり、と教室のドアを閉める。
……と。
「ぶー。なんだよー、大差ないじゃんかタイヤキもクレープもー。どっちも甘いの皮で包んでるんだからさー」
蒔寺による女の子にあるまじき暴言が聞こえてきた。
pages.en:
The classroom door slides shut behind me.

And then—

“Boo. Taiyaki, crêpes—what's the difference? They're both sweet things wrapped in dough.”

I hear Makidera utter a declaration no girl should ever make.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I shut the door behind me.
…And then,
“Man, come on! There’s no big difference between crepes and taiyaki, they’re both just sweets wrapped up!”
Makidera’s words are ones no girl should ever speak.

pages.ja:
「……タ、タイヤキとクレープが同じですって……！？」
あいつはホントに女なのか、甘いものならなんでも一緒なのか。
５００円もするフルールのベリーベリーベリーが、江戸前屋の一個８０円のタイヤキと同位などとある意味うらやましい味覚の持ち主と言えなくもないというか、 おのれ蒔寺楓、それなら初めからタイヤキで済ませておけば４２０円も得したじゃないっ……！
pages.jaRuby:
「……タ、タイヤキとクレープが同じですって……！？」
あいつはホントに女なのか、甘いものならなんでも一緒なのか。
５００円もするフルールのベリーベリーベリーが、江戸前屋の一個８０円のタイヤキと同位などとある意味うらやましい味覚の持ち主と言えなくもないというか、 おのれ蒔寺楓、それなら初めからタイヤキで済ませておけば４２０円も得したじゃないっ……！
pages.en:
“…T-Taiyaki and crêpes are the same…!?”

Is she even a woman? Does she think every sweet tastes the same?

To place Fleur's five-hundred-yen Very Very Berry crêpe on the same plane as an eighty-yen taiyaki from Edomaeya—you might almost call such a palate enviable, in its way, except—damn you, Kaede Makidera! If that was good enough, I could have bought you taiyaki from the start and saved four hundred and twenty yen…!
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Taiyaki and crepes, the same…!?”
Is she really a girl? Are all sweets the same to her?
Perhaps she just has very convenient taste buds that can’t tell a 500 yen crepe from an 80 yen taiyaki, but…
Why you… I could have saved 420 yen if I’d just bought you taiyaki to begin with…!

pages.ja:
「…………って、なに本気で悔しがってるんだわたし」
昨夜の疲れがまだ取れていないらしい。
食堂も面倒くさいし、購買でパンと飲み物を買って屋上で済ませよう。
pages.jaRuby:
「…………って、なに本気で悔しがってるんだわたし」
昨夜の疲れがまだ取れていないらしい。
食堂も面倒くさいし、購買でパンと飲み物を買って屋上で済ませよう。
pages.en:
“…………Why am I actually upset about this?”

I must still be tired from last night.

The cafeteria sounds like too much trouble. I'll buy some bread and a drink from the school store and have lunch on the roof.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Why am I getting mad about this?”
I guess I’m still tired from last night.
The cafeteria would be too much effort, so I’ll just get a drink and some bread and eat on the roof.

pages.ja:
購買でお昼ごはんを調達して、人のいない屋上に移動する。
夏場ならともかく、冬場の屋上は生徒の寄り付かない便利な場所だ。
お昼休みを取るには寒すぎるけど、まわりに気を遣わなくていいのは何事にも代えがたい。
pages.jaRuby:
購買でお昼ごはんを調達して、人のいない屋上に移動する。
夏場ならともかく、冬場の屋上は生徒の寄り付かない便利な場所だ。
お昼休みを取るには寒すぎるけど、まわりに気を遣わなくていいのは何事にも代えがたい。
pages.en:
I pick up lunch at the school store and make my way to the empty rooftop.

In summer it'd be another matter, but in winter the roof is a convenient place where no students ever venture.

It's much too cold for a comfortable lunch break, but nothing can replace the freedom of not having to mind anyone around me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I buy lunch and head for the empty rooftop.
It’s a convenient location as no student would come near it in the wintertime.
It’s too cold to eat, but that’s a small price to pay for being able to eat without worrying about other people.

pages.ja:
「さて。とりあえずごはんごはん、と」
購買のトマトサンドとホットレモンを口に運ぶ。
簡素な食事だけど、気楽に食べられる屋上だと何割か増しで美味しく感じられた。
pages.jaRuby:
「さて。とりあえずごはんごはん、と」
購買のトマトサンドとホットレモンを口に運ぶ。
簡素な食事だけど、気楽に食べられる屋上だと何割か増しで美味しく感じられた。
pages.en:
“Now then. First things first—lunch.”

I tuck into a tomato sandwich from the school store and a hot lemon drink.

It's a modest meal, but up here, where I can eat in peace, it somehow tastes considerably better.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, lunch comes first.”
I start on my tomato sandwich and hot lemon drink.
It’s a simple lunch, but the taste is much improved in this peace and quiet.

pages.ja:
「
ふう」
サンドを完食して、生暖かいホットレモンで唇を潤す。
……ちょっと疲れた。
優等生のクセに極力人付き合いを避ける、というのはバランス感覚が難しい。
pages.jaRuby:
「
ふう」
サンドを完食して、生暖かいホットレモンで唇を潤す。
……ちょっと疲れた。
優等生のクセに極力人付き合いを避ける、というのはバランス感覚が難しい。
pages.en:
“—Whew.”

I finish the sandwich and wet my lips with the lemon drink, already gone lukewarm.

…I'm a little tired.

Maintaining the life of a model student while avoiding other people wherever possible is a difficult balancing act.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Phew.”
I finish my sandwich and my hot lemon drink.
…I’m a bit tired.
It’s a difficult balance, being a good student while trying not to be too social.

pages.ja:
文武両道、学園一の優等生を守っているのはわたしの見栄というか、信念である。
どうせ学生でいるなら一番でいたいし、遠坂の名を貶めるなんてもってのほかだからだ。
そんなワケで遠坂凛は完璧な、誰から見ても隙のない女生徒をやってるワケである。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Vanity or conviction—call it what you like, but it's what keeps me at the top of the school, distinguished in academics and athletics alike.

If I'm going to be a student at all, I intend to be the best. Bringing disgrace upon the Tohsaka name is unthinkable.

And so Rin Tohsaka plays the perfect schoolgirl: impeccable, with no weakness visible to anyone.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s my vanity… no, my conviction, that I must be number-one both academically and physically.
If I am to be a student, I want to be the best, and it’s unthinkable for me to dishonor the Tohsaka name.
So that’s why I’m a perfect student, flawless in all aspects.

pages.ja:
が、同時にわたしは魔術師なんて物騒な生業をしていて、あんまり普通の人と関わるのはよろしくない。
一般人に正体を知られた魔術師は、目撃者を消す事でしか自分を守れない。
……そんなのは御免だ。
だから必然、わたしの人付き合いは簡素で表向きなものになる。
pages.jaRuby:
が、同時にわたしは魔術師なんて物騒な生業をしていて、あんまり普通の人と関わるのはよろしくない。

だから必然、わたしの人付き合いは簡素で表向きなものになる。
pages.en:
At the same time, I practice the dangerous profession of a mage. Becoming too involved with ordinary people would be unwise.

Once an outsider discovers a mage's true nature, the mage can protect herself only by eliminating the witness.

…I want no part of that.

Inevitably, then, my dealings with people remain simple and confined to the surface.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But at the same time, I also have a dangerous job as a magus, so I shouldn’t associate with normal people.
Normally, any magus whose identity is discovered has no choice but to eliminate the witness.
…I don’t want to do that.
So inevitably, my social life has become a shallow one.

pages.ja:
遊び友達の蒔寺だって休日にしか会わないし、三枝さんのように人懐っこい子の誘いも断る。
わたしは学園で一番の優等生でありながら、誰かの一番にならないように波風立てずに生活している。
それが、まあ、こんな風に疲労している時、なんとなーくつまんないなあ、と思ってしまうワケなのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
遊び友達の蒔寺だって休日にしか会わないし、三枝さんのように人懐っこい子の誘いも断る。

pages.en:
Even Makidera, the friend I go out with for fun, sees me only on holidays, and I turn down invitations from warm, openhearted girls like Saegusa.

I make my way through life without stirring up trouble—the best student in school, but careful never to become the most important person in anyone's life.

And at times like this, when I'm tired, I find myself thinking that it all feels sort of… boring.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I only hang out with Makidera on weekends, and I try to refuse invitations from friendly people like Saegusa-san.
Even though I’m the best honor student in the school, I live trying not to become too important to anyone.
Though, sometimes when I’m tired like this, it makes me think that this life is rather boring.

pages.ja:
「っと、もう時間か」
ホットレモンを飲みきって立ち上がる。
感傷にひたるのはこれぐらいにして、階段を下りたらいつもの遠坂凛に戻るとしよう
pages.jaRuby:
「っと、もう時間か」
ホットレモンを飲みきって立ち上がる。
感傷にひたるのはこれぐらいにして、階段を下りたらいつもの遠坂凛に戻るとしよう
pages.en:
“Oh. Is it that late already?”

I drain the last of the lemonade and stand.

That's enough sentimentality. Once I go downstairs, I'll be the usual Rin Tohsaka again—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, it’s time already?”
I finish my hot lemon drink and stand up.
I should stop drowning in sentimentality and go back to being the usual Tohsaka Rin once I go down the stairs

pages.ja:
「ではＨＲを終了する。日直は日誌と戸締まりの確認を。
部活動のない生徒は速やかに帰宅するように」
pages.jaRuby:
「ではＨＲを終了する。日直は日誌と戸締まりの確認を。
部活動のない生徒は速やかに帰宅するように」
pages.en:
“That concludes homeroom. The students on duty will check the class log and make sure the room is locked.

“Students without club activities are to leave school promptly.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Homeroom is at an end. Those of you on day duty, finish the daily report and check the locks.
Those of you without club activities are to go home quickly.”

pages.ja:
おきまりの台詞を残して、２年Ａ組の担任が退場する。
わたしが知る限り、今の台詞はこの一年間で一言一句違った例がない。
pages.jaRuby:
おきまりの台詞を残して、２年Ａ組の担任が退場する。
わたしが知る限り、今の台詞はこの一年間で一言一句違った例がない。
pages.en:
Our Class 2-A homeroom teacher delivers his customary lines and departs.

As far as I know, he hasn't varied so much as a single word of them all year.
pages.mirrorMoon:
2-A’s homeroom teacher exits after repeating his usual line.
As far as I know, this line hasn’t changed all year.

pages.ja:
「遠坂、今日はもうお帰り？」
「ええ。朝方間桐くんと一件あったし、面倒になる前に帰るわ」
「はは、やっぱりそうか。間桐のヤツ、今朝はとくに荒れてたからさ。遠坂に手ひどく扱われたんだろうなって思ってた」
「そう。迷惑をかけてしまったかしら、美綴さん」
「別に。間桐が下級生をいびるのはいつもの事だし。アレはアレでいい精神鍛錬になるよ」

pages.en:
“Going straight home today, Tohsaka?”

“Yes. I had a run-in with Matou this morning, so I'd like to leave before it turns into a whole thing.”

“Ha! I thought so. Matou was in an especially foul mood this morning. I figured you must have really let him have it.”

“I see. Did that cause you trouble, Mitsuzuri?”

“Not really. Matou is always tormenting the younger students. You could call it character-building.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tohsaka, you’re going home already?”
“Yes. There was an event with Matou-kun this morning, so I’m heading home before it becomes a bother.”
“Haha, I thought so. Matou was in a bad mood this morning, so I thought you must’ve given him a hard time.”
“I see. Did I cause you any trouble, Mitsuzuri-san?”
“Not at all. It’s normal for Matou to torment the younger students, and I think that kind of thing will be good mental training for him.”

pages.ja:
「そう、よかった。じゃあこの埋め合わせは、また今度」
「はいはい。これに懲りずまた寄っていってちょうだい」
pages.jaRuby:
「そう、よかった。じゃあこの埋め合わせは、また今度」
「はいはい。これに懲りずまた寄っていってちょうだい」
pages.en:
“Good. Then I'll make it up to you another time.”

“Sure, sure. Don't let this put you off stopping by again.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see, that’s good. Well, I’ll make up for it some other time.”
“All right. Don’t be put off and come by again!”

pages.ja:
寄り道をせず帰路につく。
学校から出れば、学生である遠坂凛の時間は終わりだ。
残りの半日は学生ではない自分、
遠坂の魔術師としての自分に切り替わらなくてはいけない
pages.jaRuby:

残りの半日は学生ではない自分、
遠坂の魔術師としての自分に切り替わらなくてはいけない
pages.en:
I start home without making any detours.

The moment I leave school grounds, Rin Tohsaka's time as a student comes to an end.

For the rest of the day, I must change into my other self—not a student now, but the mage of the Tohsaka family.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I head straight home.
It’s not like I don’t have any business with the archery club or the student council, but I haven’t had enough free time for them these past few days.
Once I leave school, Tohsaka Rin is no longer a student.
The rest of the day is not for myself as a student.
Instead, I must become a magus of the Tohsaka family

pages.ja:
屋敷に帰ってきたわたしを出迎えたのは、点滅する留守番電話のランプだった。
「
留守電なんて珍しいな。相手は……やっぱりアンタか、綺礼」
何を言われているか予想はつくけど、一応聞いておかないと後が怖い。
再生のボタンを押すと、聞き慣れた男の声がした。

pages.en:
The first thing to greet me when I return home to the mansion is the blinking light on the answering machine.

“A message? That's unusual. Who's it from…? Of course. You, Kirei.”

I can guess what he has to say, but the consequences of not listening would be worse.

I press Play, and a familiar man's voice fills the room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Back at my house, I’m greeted by the blinking light on my answering machine.
“It’s unusual for me to get any messages. It was… just as I thought, it’s you, Kirei.”
I already know what he’s going to say, but he’ll be scary later if I don’t listen.
When I press the play button, I hear a familiar voice.

pages.ja:
『私だ。解っていると思うが、期限は明日までだぞ凛。
あまり悠長に構えられては困る。残る席はあと二つだ。
早々にマスターを揃えねばならん』
いきなり本題を口にするあたり、この神父は容赦がない。
pages.jaRuby:
『私だ。解っていると思うが、期限は明日までだぞ凛。
あまり悠長に構えられては困る。残る席はあと二つだ。
早々にマスターを揃えねばならん』
いきなり本題を口にするあたり、この神父は容赦がない。
pages.en:
“It's me. I assume you know this already, but the deadline is tomorrow, Rin.

“I can't have you taking your time. Only two seats remain.

“We must have the Masters assembled without delay.”

Straight to the point. That priest is merciless.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s me. I’m sure you know, but tomorrow is the deadline, Rin.
It’s a problem for me if you take it easy. There are only two remaining seats.
I must ensure all the Masters are arranged quickly.”
This priest shows no mercy as he gets right to the point.

pages.ja:
『マスターの権利を放棄するというのなら今日中に連絡しろ。予備の魔術師を派遣するにも時間がかかる』
嘘つけ。予備の魔術師ぐらい、アンタならすぐに準備できるくせに。
pages.jaRuby:
『マスターの権利を放棄するというのなら今日中に連絡しろ。予備の魔術師を派遣するにも時間がかかる』
嘘つけ。予備の魔術師ぐらい、アンタならすぐに準備できるくせに。
pages.en:
“If you intend to relinquish your right to become a Master, contact me today. Even dispatching a reserve mage will take time.”

Liar. You could have a reserve mage ready in no time.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“If you wish to abandon your right to become a Master, contact me today. It takes some time to dispatch a substitute magus.”
Liar. Someone like you would be able to arrange a substitute in no time.

pages.ja:
『おまえにはすでに令呪の兆しが現れているのだ。さっさとサーヴァントを召喚し令呪を開け。
もっとも、聖杯戦争に参加しないというのならば話は別だ。命が惜しいのなら早々に教会に駆け込むがいい』
pages.jaRuby:
『おまえにはすでに令呪の兆しが現れているのだ。さっさとサーヴァントを召喚し令呪を開け。
もっとも、聖杯戦争に参加しないというのならば話は別だ。命が惜しいのなら早々に教会に駆け込むがいい』
pages.en:
“The signs of a Command Spell have already appeared upon you. Summon your Servant at once and activate your Command Spells.

“Unless, of course, you have no intention of entering the Holy Grail War. If you value your life, run to the church while you still can.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You already show signs of the Command Spell. Quickly, summon your Servant and open the Command Spell.
Unless, of course, you’re not planning to be a part of this Holy Grail War. If you value your life, you should run to the church quickly.”

pages.ja:
留守電はそこで切れた。
……簡潔と言ってはあんまりにも簡潔な言葉。
戦うなら今日中に支度しろ、戦わないのなら目障りだから早くリタイアしろ、か。
pages.jaRuby:
留守電はそこで切れた。
……簡潔と言ってはあんまりにも簡潔な言葉。
戦うなら今日中に支度しろ、戦わないのなら目障りだから早くリタイアしろ、か。
pages.en:
The message ends there.

…Calling it concise would hardly begin to cover it.

If I intend to fight, get ready today. If not, get out of the way and retire already.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The message ends there.
…His words are concise.
He’s telling me that if I am to fight, I should get ready by today and if I’m not going to fight, I’m an eyesore and should just retire quickly.

pages.ja:
「……ふん。言われなくても分かってるわよ」
まあ、こうなっちゃしょうがない。
引き延ばしも今日が限界だ。
幸い、昨日は父さんの遺言を解読できた。
戦う準備はとうに整っている。
あとは、そう
文字通り、この戦いに参加する資格を得るだけなのだが

「……ふん。言われなくても分かってるわよ」
まあ、こうなっちゃしょうがない。

pages.en:
“…Hmph. You don't have to tell me that.”

Still, there's no avoiding it now.

I can't put it off past today.

Fortunately, I deciphered Father's testament yesterday.

My preparations for battle have long been complete.

All that remains is—quite literally—to obtain the qualification required to enter this war.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Heh, you don’t have to tell me that.”
Well, it can’t be helped.
Today is as late as the deadline can be extended.
Fortunately, I was able to decode Father’s will last night.
My preparations are ready.
All that remains isyes, obtaining the qualification to enter this fight…

pages.ja:
「聖杯戦争……たった一つきりの聖杯を奪い合う殺し合い。何百年も前から伝わってきた聖杯の儀式、か……」
聖杯戦争に参加する魔術師はマスターと呼ばれる。
これは階級を表す呼称ではなく、単純に“主”としての役割を意味する。
pages.jaRuby:
「聖杯戦争……たった一つきりの聖杯を奪い合う殺し合い。何百年も前から伝わってきた聖杯の儀式、か……」
聖杯戦争に参加する魔術師はマスターと呼ばれる。
これは階級を表す呼称ではなく、単純に“主”としての役割を意味する。
pages.en:
“The Holy Grail War… A fight to the death over the one and only Holy Grail. A ritual of the Grail handed down through the centuries…”

Magi who enter the Holy Grail War are called Masters.

It is not a title of rank. It simply denotes their role as the ones in command.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“The Holy Grail War… a fight to the death for the one and only Holy Grail. A ritual of the Holy Grail passed down for hundreds of years, huh?”
The magi who participate in the Holy Grail War are called Masters.
This is not so much a rank, rather it indicates “one who is in control”.

pages.ja:
聖杯戦争に参加する条件。
それはサーヴァントと呼ばれる使い魔を召喚し、契約する事のみだ。
いくら魔術師として優れていようが、サーヴァントを従えなくてはマスターとは認められない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
There is only one condition for entering the Holy Grail War:

summon a familiar called a Servant and form a contract with it.

No matter how accomplished a mage may be, anyone who cannot command a Servant will not be recognized as a Master.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The requirement to enter the Holy Grail War.
That is to summon a familiar called a Servant, and to form a contract with it.
No matter how great a magus a person is, one is not considered a Master until he has a Servant under him.

pages.ja:
サーヴァントは通常の使い魔とは一線を画す存在だ。
その召喚、使役方法も通常の使い魔とは異なる。
聖杯戦争に参加する魔術師はこの日に備えて召喚用の触媒を用意するものなのだが……
pages.jaRuby:
サーヴァントは通常の使い魔とは一線を画す存在だ。

聖杯戦争に参加する魔術師はこの日に備えて召喚用の触媒を用意するものなのだが……
pages.en:
Servants are beings wholly distinct from ordinary familiars.

The methods by which they are summoned and controlled are different as well.

Magi intending to enter the Holy Grail War ordinarily prepare a catalyst for the summoning in anticipation of this day. But…
pages.mirrorMoon:
Servants are beings very different from normal familiars.
The methods of summoning and controlling them are different as well.
A magus planning to enter the Holy Grail War usually prepares a catalyst to summon one, but…

pages.ja:
「……ほんと。父さんもセイバーに縁の物を遺してくれれば良かったのに」
わたしには“縁”を示す品物がない。
サーヴァントは呼び出せる。
その気になれば今すぐに呼び出して契約できる。
この街の霊地は遠坂の管轄だ。
代々土地を守ってきた遠坂の跡取り娘として、他所からやってきた魔術師になんて後れはとらない。
pages.jaRuby:
「……ほんと。父さんもセイバーに縁の物を遺してくれれば良かったのに」

pages.en:
“…Honestly. Father could at least have left me something connected to Saber.”

I don't have anything that can establish that bond.

I can summon a Servant.

If I wanted to, I could summon one right now and form the contract.

The spiritual land of this city lies under Tohsaka jurisdiction.

As the daughter and heir of the family that has guarded this land for generations, I refuse to be outdone by some mage from elsewhere.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Really, I wish Father could have left me something with a connection to Saber.”
I don’t have anything with any “connection”.
I can summon a Servant.
If I wanted to, I could summon one right now and form a contract with it.
The town’s sacred ground is under our jurisdiction.
As the daughter of the Tohsaka family which has protected this town through the generations, I will not lose to magi from elsewhere.

pages.ja: とらないんだけど……流石にコンパスなしで航海には出れないというか、無計画にも程があるっていうか。
pages.jaRuby: とらないんだけど……流石にコンパスなしで航海には出れないというか、無計画にも程があるっていうか。
pages.en: I won't be. Still… even I'm not about to set sail without a compass. There's unprepared, and then there's this.
pages.mirrorMoon: But that said… I guess you can’t go out to sea without a compass. Or perhaps I should say things are completely unplanned?

pages.ja:
「……サーヴァントはシンボルによって引き寄せられる。
強力なサーヴァントを呼び出したいのなら、そのサーヴァントに縁のあるモノが必要不可欠なのだ、かぁ……」
つまり、そのサーヴァントが持っていた剣とか鎧とか、紋章とか骨とか、そういうとんでもない値打ち物だ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……サーヴァントはシンボルによって引き寄せられる。
強力なサーヴァントを呼び出したいのなら、そのサーヴァントに縁のあるモノが必要不可欠なのだ、かぁ……」
つまり、そのサーヴァントが持っていた剣とか鎧とか、紋章とか骨とか、そういうとんでもない値打ち物だ。
pages.en:
“…Servants are drawn to symbols.

“If I want to summon a powerful Servant, I absolutely need something tied to them…”

In other words, a sword or suit of armor they once used, a crest, a bone—some absurdly valuable relic like that.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Servants are attracted to symbols.
If you want to summon a strong Servant, you need something that has a connection to that Servant.”
In other words, a sword, armor, talisman, bone of that Servant, or something like that… something valuable beyond belief.

pages.ja:
「……父さんの遺言に期待してたんだけどなあ……ううん、これはこれでもの凄い切り札なんだけど」
昨夜地下室で発見したペンダントは、古代遺物としては最上級の代物だ。
これはこれで凄い。
凄いんだけど、サーヴァント召喚の役には立たない。
pages.jaRuby:
「……父さんの遺言に期待してたんだけどなあ……ううん、これはこれでもの凄い切り札なんだけど」
昨夜地下室で発見したペンダントは、[ruby text=アーティファクト char=4]古代遺物としては最上級の代物だ。
これはこれで凄い。
凄いんだけど、サーヴァント召喚の役には立たない。
pages.en:
“…I really had my hopes up about Father's testament… No—this is an incredible trump card in its own right.”

The pendant I found in the basement last night is an artifact of the highest order—an ancient relic.

It is extraordinary. Truly.

But it is no use at all in summoning a Servant.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I was hoping there’d be something like that in Father’s will, but… No, this is a great trump card too. But still…”
The pendant I found last night in the basement is one of the best Artifacts in its class.
It’s great in its own way.
It’s great, but it won’t help me to summon my servant.

pages.ja: 「……ふん。いいわよ、そんな物に頼らなくたってなんとかなるわ。そもそも、わたし以外にセイバーを扱えるマスターなんている筈ないし」
pages.jaRuby: 「……ふん。いいわよ、そんな物に頼らなくたってなんとかなるわ。そもそも、わたし以外にセイバーを扱えるマスターなんている筈ないし」
pages.en: “…Hmph. Fine. I can manage without relying on anything like that. Besides, there cannot possibly be another Master capable of handling Saber.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Huh! It’s fine. I can do it without help from that sort of thing. After all, there can’t exist any Masters capable of handling Saber other than myself.”

pages.ja:
よし、決めた。
これ以上延ばして綺礼に嫌みを言われるのもご免だし、ギリギリまで待つなんて性に合わない。
こうなったら本番勝負。
今夜万全の態勢でサーヴァント召喚に臨んで、力ずくでセイバーを手に入れてやるんだから……！
pages.jaRuby:
よし、決めた。
これ以上延ばして綺礼に嫌みを言われるのもご免だし、ギリギリまで待つなんて性に合わない。
こうなったら本番勝負。
今夜万全の態勢でサーヴァント召喚に臨んで、力ずくでセイバーを手に入れてやるんだから……！
pages.en:
—All right. I've made up my mind.

I refuse to put this off any longer and give Kirei another chance to sneer at me. Waiting until the very last moment does not suit me either.

So this is it—the real thing.

Tonight I'll make every preparation, perform the summoning, and drag Saber here by force if I have to…!
pages.mirrorMoon:
All right, I’ve decided.
I don’t want to make Kirei complain any more by postponing it any longer, and it’s not like me to wait until the last second.
It’ll come down to just trying it.
I’ll face the summoning tonight with full power and obtain Saber by force…!

pages.ja:
深夜。
時計の針はじき午前二時を指そうとしている。
わたしにとって最も波長のいい時間帯。
その中でもピークになるのが午前二時ジャスト。
制限的にもこれが最初にして最後のチャンスだから、わずかでもミスをする訳にはいかない。
pages.jaRuby:
深夜。
時計の針はじき午前二時を指そうとしている。
わたしにとって最も波長のいい時間帯。
その中でもピークになるのが午前二時ジャスト。
制限的にもこれが最初にして最後のチャンスだから、わずかでもミスをする訳にはいかない。
pages.en:
The dead of night.

The clock will soon strike two in the morning.

This is when I'm most closely attuned to my wavelength.

I reach my peak at exactly two.

Given the time limit, this is my first and last chance. I can't afford even the slightest mistake.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Late at night.
The clock is about to strike two.
This is the best timeframe for my magical energy.
The peak of my magical energy is at exactly two in the morning.
Since this will be my first and last chance, I can’t afford any mistakes.

pages.ja:
「
消去の中に退去、退去の陣を四つ刻んで召喚の陣で囲む、と」
pages.jaRuby:
「
消去の中に退去、退去の陣を四つ刻んで召喚の陣で囲む、と」
pages.en: “Banishment within erasure. Inscribe four arrays of banishment, then enclose them within the summoning array.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Withdrawal within elimination, engrave four areas and surround with the summoning circle… right.”

pages.ja:
地下室の床に陣を刻む。
……実際、サーヴァント召喚にはさして大がかりな降霊は必要ない。
サーヴァントは聖杯によって招かれるモノ。
マスターは彼らをつなぎ止め、実体化に必要な魔力を提供する事が第一なのだから、召喚はあちらが勝手にやってくれる。
pages.jaRuby:
地下室の床に陣を刻む。
……実際、サーヴァント召喚にはさして大がかりな降霊は必要ない。
サーヴァントは聖杯によって招かれるモノ。
マスターは彼らをつなぎ止め、実体化に必要な魔力を提供する事が第一なのだから、召喚はあちらが勝手にやってくれる。
pages.en:
I carve the array into the basement floor.

…In truth, summoning a Servant requires no particularly elaborate spirit ritual.

The Holy Grail is what calls the Servant. A Master's main job is to anchor the Servant here and supply the magical energy they need to take form. The Grail handles the actual summoning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I engrave the circle onto the floor of the basement.
You don’t need a large-scale summoning to summon the Servant.
Servants are called forth by the Holy Grail.
As the Master’s priority is to keep the Servant in this world and to supply them with enough magical energy to substantiate, the Holy Grail takes care of the summoning.

pages.ja:
「素に銀と鉄。礎に石と契約の大公。祖には我が大師シュバインオーグ。
降り立つ風には壁を。四方の門は閉じ、王冠より出で、王国に至る三叉路は循環せよ」
pages.jaRuby:
「素に銀と鉄。礎に石と契約の大公。祖には我が大師シュバインオーグ。
降り立つ風には壁を。四方の門は閉じ、王冠より出で、王国に至る三叉路は循環せよ」
pages.en:
“Let silver and iron be the essence. Let stone and the Archduke of Contracts be the foundation. Let my great master Schweinorg be the forebear.

“Let a wall rise against the descending wind. Let the gates in every direction close. From the crown, let the three-forked road to the kingdom revolve.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Bare and silver and iron. Stone for foundation and the Grand Duke of contracts. My great master Schweinorg for the ancestor.
A wall for the descending winds. The four gates shall close and come out the crown. Let the three-forked road to the kingdom cycle.”

pages.ja:
それでも、細心の注意と努力を。
本来なら血液で描く魔法陣を、今回は溶解した宝石で描く。
……わたしが今までため込んできた宝石のうち半分を使うんだから、財政的にも失敗なんて承知しない。
pages.jaRuby:
それでも、細心の注意と努力を。
本来なら血液で描く魔法陣を、今回は溶解した宝石で描く。
……わたしが今までため込んできた宝石のうち半分を使うんだから、財政的にも失敗なんて承知しない。
pages.en:
Even so, I take every possible precaution and spare no effort.

The circle would ordinarily be drawn in blood. This time, I draw it in liquefied jewels.

…I'm using half the jewels I've spent years stockpiling. I can't afford to fail—literally.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Still, I continue with the greatest concentration.
I draw the magic circle, normally written in blood, with my melted jewels.
…I’m using half the jewels I’ve saved up, so I can’t fail for financial reasons too.

pages.ja:
「閉じよ。閉じよ。閉じよ。閉じよ。閉じよ。
繰り返すつどに五度。
ただ、満たされる刻を破却する」
pages.jaRuby:
「[ruby text=みたせ o2o=1]閉じよ。[ruby text=みたせ o2o=1]閉じよ。[ruby text=みたせ o2o=1]閉じよ。[ruby text=みたせ o2o=1]閉じよ。[ruby text=みたせ o2o=1]閉じよ。
繰り返すつどに五度。
ただ、満たされる刻を破却する」
pages.en:
“Close and fill. Close and fill. Close and fill. Close and fill. Close and fill.

“Repeat it five times.

“Only, let the hour of fulfillment be destroyed.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Enclose. Enclose. Enclose. Enclose. Enclose.
Five times for each repetition.
Just destroy the enclosed time.”

pages.ja:
……じき午前二時。
遠坂の家に伝わる召喚陣を描き終え、全霊をもって対峙する。
pages.jaRuby:
……じき午前二時。
遠坂の家に伝わる召喚陣を描き終え、全霊をもって対峙する。
pages.en:
…It will soon be two in the morning.

The Tohsaka summoning circle is complete. I gather everything I have and face it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…It’s almost two in the morning.
Completing the magic circle passed down through the Tohsaka family, I face it with all my power.

pages.ja:
「
Anfang」
わたしの中にある、カタチのないスイッチをオンにする。
かちり、と体の中身が入れ替わるような感覚。
通常の神経が反転して、魔力を伝わらせる回路へと切り替わる。
これより遠坂凛は人ではなく。
ただ、神秘を成し得る為だけの部品となる。
pages.jaRuby:
「
[ruby text=セット char=6]Anfang」
わたしの中にある、カタチのないスイッチをオンにする。
かちり、と体の中身が入れ替わるような感覚。
通常の神経が反転して、魔力を伝わらせる回路へと切り替わる。
これより遠坂凛は人ではなく。
ただ、神秘を成し得る為だけの部品となる。
pages.en:
“Set.”

I throw the formless switch inside me.

Click. It feels as though everything inside me has been swapped out.

My ordinary nerves invert, switching over into circuits through which magical energy can flow.

From this moment on, Rin Tohsaka is no longer human.

She is nothing more than a component made for the sole purpose of bringing mystery into being.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Anfang.”
I flip the formless switch inside me.
I feel a sensation as if the contents of my body are being exchanged.
The usual nerves invert into circuits transmitting magical energy.
From this point, Tohsaka Rin is not human.
I shall become a tool to attain mystic power.

pages.ja:
……指先から溶けていく。
否、指先から満たされていく。
取り込むマナがあまりにも濃密だから、もとからあった肉体の感覚が塗りつぶされていく。
だから、満たされるという事は、同時に破却するという事だ。
pages.jaRuby:
……指先から溶けていく。
否、指先から満たされていく。
取り込むマナがあまりにも濃密だから、もとからあった肉体の感覚が塗りつぶされていく。
だから、満たされるという事は、同時に破却するという事だ。
pages.en:
…I begin to melt from the fingertips inward.

No. I begin to fill from the fingertips inward.

The Mana pouring into me is so dense that it paints over every sensation of the body I had before.

And so, to be filled is, at the same time, to be destroyed.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I am melting from my fingertips.
No, I am being filled from my fingertips.
The mana I am taking in is so concentrated that the original senses of my body are being repainted.
So, being filled is the same as being destroyed.

pages.ja:
「
」
全身に行き渡る力は、大気に含まれる純然たる魔力。
これを回路となった自身に取り込み、違う魔力へと変換する。
魔術師の体は回路にすぎない。
幽体と物質を繋げる為の回路。
その結果、成し得た様々な神秘を、我々は魔術と呼ぶ。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
全身に行き渡る力は、大気に含まれる純然たる魔力。
これを回路となった自身に取り込み、違う魔力へと変換する。
魔術師の体は回路にすぎない。
幽体と物質を繋げる為の回路。
その結果、成し得た様々な神秘を、我々は魔術と呼ぶ。
pages.en:
“—”

The force suffusing my body is pure magical energy contained in the atmosphere.

I take it into the body that has become a circuit and convert it into another kind of magical energy.

A mage's body is nothing more than a circuit—

a circuit for joining spirit to matter.

The many mysteries made possible through that connection are what we call magecraft.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
The power that fills me is pure magical energy from the air.
It is absorbed by my body, which has become a circuit, and transformed into a different form of magical energy.
The body of a magus is nothing more than a circuit.
A circuit to connect the spiritual and the real.
We call the result of this, the many mystic occurrences it has made real, magic.

pages.ja:
……体が熱い。
額に角が生えるような錯覚。
背に羽が生えるような錯覚。
手に鱗が生えるような錯覚。
踝に水が満ちるような感覚。
……汗が滲む。
ザクン、ザクン、と体中に剣が突き刺さる。
pages.jaRuby:
……体が熱い。
額に角が生えるような錯覚。
背に羽が生えるような錯覚。
手に鱗が生えるような錯覚。
踝に水が満ちるような感覚。
……汗が滲む。
ザクン、ザクン、と体中に剣が突き刺さる。
pages.en:
…My body is burning.

The illusion of a horn growing from my brow.

The illusion of wings growing from my back.

The illusion of scales spreading across my hands.

The sensation of water closing over my ankles.

…Sweat beads on my skin.

One after another, swords drive themselves into every part of my body.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…My body is burning hot.
An illusion of myself growing horns.
An illusion of wings growing out of my back.
An illusion of scales forming on my hands.
A sensation of being in water.
…I start to sweat.
Stab, stab. Swords are driven into my body.

pages.ja:
それは人であるわたしの体が、魔術回路と成っているわたしの体を嫌う聖痕だ。
いかに優れた魔術師であろうと人は人。
この痛みは、人の身で魔術を使うかぎり永劫につきまとう。
pages.jaRuby:
それは人であるわたしの体が、魔術回路と成っているわたしの体を嫌う聖痕だ。
いかに優れた魔術師であろうと人は人。
この痛みは、人の身で魔術を使うかぎり永劫につきまとう。
pages.en:
That pain is a stigma: my human body rejecting the body I have turned into Magic Circuits.

However accomplished a mage may be, a human remains human.

So long as we work magecraft in bodies of flesh, this pain will pursue us forever.
pages.mirrorMoon:
This is the pain caused by my human body rejecting itself as the Magic Circuit.
No matter how great a magus you are, a human is human.
This pain will result as long as people use magic in a human body.

pages.ja:

It crawls through my body, scraping and gnawing like a fanged centipede—

The harvested mana in my blood.
If that is burning iron, then the Magic Crest itself is like a nerve made of thorns.
It runs through my body like a centipede with fangs

“—”

The pain drives me out of myself.

At the same time, I feel it: I've reached the place I was aiming for.

My sharpened hearing catches the clock ticking in the living room.

Ten seconds remain until two.

The power filling my body is flawless now.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I lose myself within that pain.
And at the same time, I feel that I have reached my goal.
My overly sensitive hearing keeps recognizing the sound of the clock in the living room.
Ten more seconds until two in the morning.
The power within me is perfect and flawless.

I take the mana I’ve absorbed and turn it into “fixed” magical energy.
And now…
I have only to empty out the mana within me to move the engine called the summoning circle…

Thy body shall be under my command, my fate shall be determined by thy sword.
Follow the call of the Holy Grail. If thou wouldst obey this mind and this reason, then answer my call.”

My sight closes.

Before me looms the fifth element, which no naked eye can perceive.

Fearing it will be crushed, my sight shuts itself down.
pages.mirrorMoon:
My vision closes.
The fifth element, said to be unperceivable by human eyes, is before me.
So, in fear of being broken by it, vision shuts itself down.

pages.ja:

我は常世総ての善と成る者、
我は常世総ての悪を敷く者。
汝三大の言霊を纏う七天、
抑止の輪より来たれ、天秤の守り手よ
！」

pages.en:
“Here I make my oath.

“I shall become all the good of the eternal world.

“I shall hold dominion over all the evil of the eternal world.

“You, seven heavens clad in the three great words of power,

“come forth from the ring of restraint, O guardian of the scales!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Make an oath here.
I am the one who shall become the virtue of all afterworld.
I am the one who shall lay out the evil of all afterworld.
Thou art Seven Heavens clad in the Three Great Words.
Emerge from the ring of control, guardian of balance…!”

pages.ja:

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Flawless…!

The pull on the line is perfect—like reeling in a whale with a fishing rod!

Perfect…!

Another few seconds and my eyes will recover. Then, right before me, the Servant I summoned will be—

Perfect…! I’ve drawn the strongest card for sure…!
“Perfect…! I’ve drawn the strongest card for sure…!”
Geez, I can’t wait for my vision to return.
My vision should recover in a matter of seconds and there will be the summoned Servant right in front of me…

pages.ja: ない。

pages.en: —nowhere.
pages.mirrorMoon: Nothing.

pages.ja:
「はい……？」
ないものはない。
変化なんてこれっぽっちもない。
あんだけ派手にエーテルを乱舞させておいて、実体化しているモノが欠片もない。
加えて。

“Excuse me…?”

There's nothing. Nothing at all.

Not the slightest thing has changed.

After all that spectacular ether whirling through the air, not so much as a scrap has taken form.

And on top of that—

something has just exploded in the living room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh…?”
Nothing is nothing.
There is no change.
I’ve raged out that much ether and nothing has formed.
And on top of that…
I hear an explosion from the living room.

pages.ja:
「なんでよーーーーー！？」
走った。
もう頭んなか空っぽにしたまま走った。
地下室の階段を駆け上がって居間へ急ぐ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Whyyyyyyy!?”

I run.

Mind completely blank, I run.

I charge up the basement stairs and race toward the living room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“WHY!!!!?”
I run.
I keep running without thinking.
I run up the basement stairs and into the living room.

The living-room door is warped.

The handle does nothing.

The door won't budge, no matter which way I shove it, so—

“Oh, get out of my way, you—!”

The living room door is crooked.
There’s no point in turning the handle.
The door doesn’t open, even as I push and pull it.
“…Geez, you’re in my way…!”
With a crash, I kick through the door into the living room.

And then.

The instant I enter the living room, I understand everything.

And.
The instant I walk into the living room, I understand everything.

アレ、間違いなく下手人だ。

“……………”

No question who did it.

“……”

破壊を免れた柱時計は正確に時間を刻んでいる。
……それで、思い出してしまった。
うん、そうそう。たしかうちの時計、今日にかぎって一時間早かったんだっけ。
つまり今は午前一時。
わたしの絶好調まで、ほんとはあと一時間。

The grandfather clock, spared from the destruction, is still ticking away with perfect regularity.

Yes. That's right. Today of all days, every clock in the house is an hour fast.

Which means it's actually one in the morning.

I still have another hour before I reach my peak.

“……”
But there’s one thing more important than that.
The wall clock is still ticking away time, having escaped destruction.
…That reminds me.
Yes, that’s right. Come to think of it, every clock in my house was an hour early today for some reason.
In other words, it’s one in the morning right now.
There’s actually one more hour until my magical energy is at its peak.

pages.jaRuby:

I can do most things just like everyone else, but I have one hereditary curse.
That is, to make the biggest mistakes at the most important times…

自分の馬鹿さ加減が腹立たしい。

My own stupidity infuriates me.

Still bristling with irritation, I glare at the man sprawled imperiously across the rubble.

I am mad at my own stupidity.
Still irritated, I glare at the man sitting there like he’s important.

“Those are your first words to me? What an extraordinary Master I've been saddled with.”

This man has a thoroughly twisted personality.

The man in red gives an exaggerated shrug.

Just standing here, I can tell this thing has outrageous amounts of magical energy.
Don’t be fooled by its appearance.
This is certainly an existence far beyond human, a “ghost” that has reached the level of spirits as a human.

pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I can’t be overwhelmed forever.
That thing is mine.
So, I’ll have to change my thinking from now on.

pages.ja:
「
確認するけど、貴方はわたしのサーヴァントで間違いない？」

「……そうか。だが私が召喚された時に、君は目の前にいなかった。これはどういう事なのか説明してくれ」

“Are you serious? You aren't a baby chick. Don't tell me you can decide who your Master is only by who happens to be there when you open your eyes.”

“I see. But when I was summoned, you were not in front of me. Explain to me what’s going on.”
“Really? Don’t joke around and tell me you’re like a newborn chick who can only determine your Master when you open your eyes.”

pages.ja:
む、と正体不明のサーヴァントは顔をしかめた。
こっちの言い分に腹が立ったのか、それともあんまりにもわたしの言葉が正しかったから感心したのか、ちょっと微妙な反応だ。

It's difficult to tell whether my argument has angered him or whether he's simply impressed by how completely right I am.

It’s a rather vague response, and I cannot tell if he’s angry at my complaint or impressed at how correct I am.

まあ、後のことは私に任せて、君は自分の身の安全、を……！？」
「あったまきたぁーーーーー！
いいわ、そんなに言うなら使ってやろうじゃない！」
pages.en:
“You cannot use a Command Spell in any case.

“Leave everything else to me. Your only concern should be your own safet—”

“That's it! My blood is boiling!

“Fine! If that's how you want it, then I'll use one!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You wouldn’t be able to use the Command Spell anyway.
Well, you can leave the rest to me. You just worry about your own safe…ty…!?”
“I’m pissed!
Fine, if you say that, I’ll use it!”

pages.ja:
「
Anfang……！」
もう容赦なしだ、こんな捻くれモノ相手にかけてやる情けなんてあるもんかっ……！

pages.en:
“Set…!”

No more mercy. Why should I spare a shred of compassion for someone this twisted…!?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Anfang…!”
There’s no holding back now. I’ve no sympathy for a twisted guy like him…!

pages.ja:

まさか……！？」
「そのまさかよこの礼儀知らず！
Vertrag……！ Ein neuer Nagel Ein neues Gesetz Ein neues Verbrechen
！」

！」
pages.en:
“What—you cannot possibly…!?”

“I most certainly can, you ill-mannered brute!

“Command Spell, hear me…! By the laws of the Holy Grail, bind this one as my Servant and lay another law of restraint upon him!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wha… you’re not…!?”
“Exactly what you’re thinking, you rude scum!
Vertrag…! Ein neuer Nagel. Ein neues Gesetz. Ein neues Verbrechen!”
(I announce to the Command Spell! By the order of the Holy Grail, give the law of obedience to this one, my Servant!)

pages.ja:
「ば…………！？ 待て、正気かマスター！？ そんなコトで令呪を使うヤツが……！」
「うるさーい！
いい、アンタはわたしのサーヴァント！ なら、わたしの言い分には絶対服従ってもんでしょうーーー！？」
pages.jaRuby:
「ば…………！？ 待て、正気かマスター！？ そんなコトで令呪を使うヤツが……！」

いい、アンタはわたしのサーヴァント！ なら、わたしの言い分には絶対服従ってもんでしょうーーー！？」
pages.en:
“Y-you…!? Wait! Have you lost your mind, Master!? Who would use a Command Spell over something like—?”

“Be quiet!

“Listen to me! You are my Servant! And that means absolute obedience to every word I say!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You idi…! Wait, are you insane, Master!? Who would use the Command Spell for something like this…!”
“Shut up!
Look, you’re my Servant! You have to obey every single one of my orders, okay!?”
“W-What…!?”

pages.ja:
右手に刻まれた印が疼く。
三つの令呪。
聖杯戦争の要、サーヴァントを律するという三つの絶対命令権が行使される。
pages.jaRuby:
右手に刻まれた印が疼く。
三つの令呪。
聖杯戦争の要、サーヴァントを律するという三つの絶対命令権が行使される。
pages.en:
The mark engraved upon my right hand begins to throb.

Three Command Spells.

The heart of the Holy Grail War: three absolute commands with the power to bind a Servant. One of them is set in motion.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The symbol on my right hand throbs.
The three Command Spells.
The essence of the Holy Grail War, the three claims to the Servant’s unconditional obedience, is now used.

pages.ja:
「か、考えなしか君は……！ こ、こんな大雑把な事に令呪を使うなど……！」
ふん、怒鳴られても後の祭りよ。
……だいたい、わたしだって予想外だ。
自己嫌悪で死にたくなる。
まさかこんなコトで、大事な令呪をあっさりと使うハメになるなんて
！
pages.jaRuby:
「か、考えなしか君は……！ こ、こんな大雑把な事に令呪を使うなど……！」

！
pages.en:
“D-do you ever think!? Using a Command Spell on an order that broad…!”

Hmph. It's too late for shouting now.

…This was hardly what I expected either.

I could die of self-disgust.

How did I let myself be driven into squandering a precious Command Spell so casually over something like this…!?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“A-Are you not even thinking…! Using the Command Spell for such a general thing…!”
Huh, it’s too late now.
…First of all, I wasn’t expecting this either.
I hate myself so much, I want to die.
To go ahead and use the important Command Spell for something like this…!

pages.ja:
で。
廃墟みたいになった居間から引き上げて、とりあえず私の部屋に移動した。
目の前にはわたしの令呪で“絶対服従”になったはずのサーヴァントがいる。
いるんだけど

pages.en:
And so—

I withdraw from the living room, now indistinguishable from a ruin, and move into my bedroom for the time being.

Standing before me is the Servant whom my Command Spell has supposedly reduced to “absolute obedience.”

Except—
pages.mirrorMoon:
So.
Leaving the ruined living room behind, we move to my room.
In front of me is the Servant who should be “absolutely obedient” from my Command Spell.
He’s there, but…

pages.ja:
「……なるほど。君の性質はだいたい理解したぞ、マスター」
これの、どこが絶対服従なんだって言うのかっ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……なるほど。君の性質はだいたい理解したぞ、マスター」
これの、どこが絶対服従なんだって言うのかっ。
pages.en:
“…I see. I believe I understand your character now, Master.”

How is this supposed to count as absolute obedience?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see. I understand your personality now, Master.”
How exactly is this “absolutely obedient”?

pages.ja:
「念のため訊ねるが。君は令呪がどれほど重要か理解しているのか、マスター」
「し、知ってるわよ。サーヴァントを律する三回きりの命令権でしょ。それがなによ」
pages.jaRuby:
「念のため訊ねるが。君は令呪がどれほど重要か理解しているのか、マスター」
「し、知ってるわよ。サーヴァントを律する三回きりの命令権でしょ。それがなによ」
pages.en:
“Just to be certain, I must ask: do you understand the importance of a Command Spell, Master?”

“O-of course I do. It gives a Master three—and only three—chances to command a Servant. What of it?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Just to make sure… do you understand how important the Command Spell is, Master?”
“I-I know. It’s the right to give your Servant three orders, right? What about it?”

pages.ja:
「……はあ。いいかね、令呪はサーヴァントを強制的に行動させるものだ。
それは“行動を止める”だけでなく、“行動を強化させる”という意味でもある」
pages.jaRuby:
「……はあ。いいかね、令呪はサーヴァントを強制的に行動させるものだ。
それは“行動を止める”だけでなく、“行動を強化させる”という意味でもある」
pages.en:
“…Hah. Listen carefully. A Command Spell compels a Servant to act.

“Its power can be used not only to stop an action, but to reinforce one.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Geez. Look, the Command Spell forces the Servant to act according to an order.
It doesn’t merely stop their actions, it strengthens their actions as well.”

pages.ja:
「例えば、私はここから遠くの場所まで瞬間的には移動できない。だが令呪で“行け”と命じれば、それが私と君の魔力で届く事ならば可能となる。
強制命令権とはそういう事だ。サーヴァント自身でも制御できない、肉体の限界さえ突破させる大魔術の結晶が三つの令呪なのだ。まあ、今では二つに減ってしまったがな」
pages.jaRuby:
「例えば、私はここから遠くの場所まで瞬間的には移動できない。だが令呪で“行け”と命じれば、それが私と君の魔力で届く事ならば可能となる。
強制命令権とはそういう事だ。サーヴァント自身でも制御できない、肉体の限界さえ突破させる大魔術の結晶が三つの令呪なのだ。まあ、今では二つに減ってしまったがな」
pages.en:
“For example, I cannot move instantaneously from here to some distant place. But if a Command Spell ordered me to go, the feat would become possible—provided our combined magical energy could carry me that far.

“That is the nature of absolute command. The three Command Spells are crystallizations of grand magecraft, capable of forcing a Servant's body past limits even the Servant cannot overcome unaided. Though you now possess only two.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“For example, I can’t instantly teleport to somewhere far away. But if you command me to ‘go’ using your Command Spell, then assuming we have enough magical energy, such things become possible.
This is what is meant by unconditional obedience. It is the three crystallizations of a great magic that allows a Servant to surpass limits on their ability even they can’t control. Well, only two now.”

pages.ja: 「し、知ってるわよそんなコト。いいじゃない、まだ二つあるんだし、貴方に命じた規則は無駄じゃないんだし」
pages.jaRuby: 「し、知ってるわよそんなコト。いいじゃない、まだ二つあるんだし、貴方に命じた規則は無駄じゃないんだし」
pages.en: “I-I know all that. It's fine. I still have two, and the rule I imposed on you wasn't meaningless.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I-I know that. It’s fine, we still have two and that order I gave you isn’t useless, either.”

pages.ja:
「……ふう。確かに、これは私の誤算だった。
令呪というものは曖昧な命令には効きが弱くなる。
“私を守りとおせ”“この戦いに勝て”などといった、広く長く効果が続くものには令呪の力が弱くなる。強制は長く続くが、苦痛が小さい為逆らえるサーヴァントも出てくるだろう」
pages.jaRuby:
「……ふう。確かに、これは私の誤算だった。
令呪というものは曖昧な命令には効きが弱くなる。
“私を守りとおせ”“この戦いに勝て”などといった、広く長く効果が続くものには令呪の力が弱くなる。[ruby text=ききめ char=2]強制は長く続くが、苦痛が小さい為逆らえるサーヴァントも出てくるだろう」
pages.en:
“…Hah. That, admittedly, was my miscalculation.

“The more ambiguous an order, the weaker a Command Spell becomes.

“Broad, long-term commands such as ‘protect me to the end’ or ‘win this war’ dilute its power. The compulsion itself persists, but the pain it inflicts is slight enough that some Servants will be able to resist.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Man. This was certainly a miscalculation on my part.
The Command Spell works poorly on broad orders.
For broad and long-lasting orders like ‘protect me through this’ or ‘win this battle’, the power of the Command Spell weakens. The force will last a long time, but since the associated pain is weak, some Servants will be able to disobey.”

pages.ja:
「逆に、“次の一撃を死ぬ気で放て”“あのグラスだけは壊すな”といった単一の命令は絶対で、よほど強力なサーヴァントでも逆らうのは難しくなる。
……さて。ここまでで私が言いたい事がわかるな、マスター」
pages.jaRuby:
「逆に、“次の一撃を死ぬ気で放て”“あのグラスだけは壊すな”といった単一の命令は絶対で、よほど強力なサーヴァントでも逆らうのは難しくなる。
……さて。ここまでで私が言いたい事がわかるな、マスター」
pages.en:
“Conversely, a single, specific command—‘put your life into your next blow,’ or ‘do not break that glass’—is absolute. Even an exceptionally powerful Servant would find it difficult to resist.

“…By now, you understand my point, Master.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“In contrast, a single, simple order like ‘deliver the next blow with all your power’, or ‘don’t break that glass’ is absolute, and even the most powerful Servants will find it hard to disobey.
…So, I think you can guess what I’d like to say next, Master.”

pages.ja:
「……解るわよ。ようするに、広く長い命令は意味がないんでしょ。
効果も戒めも薄いなら、サーヴァントは令呪に逆らって行動できる。そんな効き目の薄い命令をするなら、絶対的な“単一の命令”をした方がいい」
pages.jaRuby:
「……解るわよ。ようするに、広く長い命令は意味がないんでしょ。
効果も[ruby text=いまし]戒めも薄いなら、サーヴァントは令呪に逆らって行動できる。そんな効き目の薄い命令をするなら、絶対的な“単一の命令”をした方がいい」
pages.en:
“…I understand. Broad commands that last a long time are pointless.

“If both the effect and the restraint are weak, a Servant can defy the Command Spell and act freely. Rather than give an order that feeble, you should issue one absolute, singular command.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I get the idea. So you’re saying a broad, long-lasting order is meaningless, right?
If the effect is weak, Servants can act against it. It’s better to make a single absolute order than to give weak ones, right?”

pages.ja:
「そうだ。令呪とは元々、自分たちの能力以上の奇跡を起こす為のもの。それを代用の効く命令などで消費する愚は許されない。
……君の先ほどの令呪はまさにそれだ。私が君に従うかは話し合いで解決できた事だし、仮に令呪を使ったところで“全ての言動に絶対服従”など、令呪が百あっても実現できない」
pages.jaRuby:
「そうだ。令呪とは元々、自分たちの能力以上の奇跡を起こす為のもの。それを代用の効く命令などで消費する愚は許されない。
……君の先ほどの令呪はまさにそれだ。私が君に従うかは話し合いで解決できた事だし、仮に令呪を使ったところで“全ての言動に絶対服従”など、令呪が百あっても実現できない」
pages.en:
“Precisely. Command Spells exist to produce miracles beyond the abilities of Master and Servant alike. To squander one on an order that could be achieved by other means is unforgivable folly.

“Your command just now is the perfect example. Whether I would obey you was something we could have settled by talking. And even with a Command Spell, ‘absolute obedience in every word and deed’ would remain impossible if you possessed a hundred of them.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Right. Basically, the Command Spell is a way to bring about miracles beyond our abilities. Stupidly using it for orders that can be achieved by other means is unforgivable.
The Command Spell you just used is exactly that. Whether or not I’ll obey you is something that we could have solved by discussion. Even with the command, something like ‘obey my every order completely’ is beyond even a hundred Command Spells.”

pages.ja:
「う……じゃあ、わたしのさっきの令呪は無意味って事……？」
「……通常ならそうなのだがな。どうも、君の魔術師としての性能はケタが違ったらしい」
「？」
呆れているのか、嬉しいのか。
サーヴァントは溜息をつきながらも、口元を緩ませている。
pages.jaRuby:
「う……じゃあ、わたしのさっきの令呪は無意味って事……？」

pages.en:
“Urk… Then the Command Spell I just used was meaningless…?”

“…Ordinarily, yes. It appears, however, that your ability as a mage is on an entirely different order of magnitude.”

“?”

Whether from exasperation or pleasure, the Servant sighs, yet the corners of his mouth lift into a faint smile.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ugh… so the Command Spell I just used was meaningless…?”
“…Normally, the answer would be yes. But it seems that your abilities as a magus are on a completely different level.”
“…?”
Is he happy or unhappy?
The Servant has a smile on his face as he sighs.

pages.ja:
「ケタが違ったって
もしかして。
ちょっと貴方。自分が今どんな状態なのか、正直に話してみなさい」
ピンとくるものがあって、ちょっと強気に訊いてみる。
pages.jaRuby:
「ケタが違ったって
もしかして。
ちょっと貴方。自分が今どんな状態なのか、正直に話してみなさい」
ピンとくるものがあって、ちょっと強気に訊いてみる。
pages.en:
“An entirely different order of magnitude—wait. Does that mean…?

“You. Tell me honestly what condition you're in right now.”

An idea comes to me, and I press him with renewed confidence.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“On a completely different level… you mean…
Hey, you. Tell me honestly your condition right now.”
I have a gut feeling, so I ask him boldly.

pages.ja:
「ああ。誤算というのはそれだ。
先ほどの令呪では、“少しはマスターの意見を尊重しよう”という程度の心変わりにしかならない。
だが、今の私は君の言葉に強い強制を感じている。君の意見に異を唱えると、そうだな……ランクが一つばかり落ちるようだ。
つまり、マスターの意向に逆らうと体が重くなって動き辛い、というところか」
困ったものだ、と肩をすくめるサーヴァント。
pages.jaRuby:
「ああ。誤算というのはそれだ。
先ほどの[ruby text=めいれい char=2]令呪では、“少しはマスターの意見を尊重しよう”という程度の心変わりにしかならない。

困ったものだ、と肩をすくめるサーヴァント。
pages.en:
“Yes. That was my miscalculation.

“Ordinarily, the Command Spell you used would produce no more than a change of heart—a vague inclination to show a little respect for my Master's opinions.

“But now I feel a powerful compulsion behind your words. Whenever I go against your judgment, it feels as though my abilities drop by about one rank.

“In other words, whenever I act against my Master's wishes, my body grows heavy and difficult to move.”

What a nuisance, his shrug seems to say.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah, that’s what I mean by miscalculation.
That Command Spell should have only changed my attitude to ‘well, I’ll respect Master’s opinions slightly’.
But right now, I feel a strong bind from your words. If I disagree with you, let’s see… it seems like I drop a rank.
In other words, it’s like my body feels heavy when I go against your will.”
The Servant shrugs his shoulders as if to say it’s a pain.

pages.ja:
「
えっと」
……って事は、さっきの令呪は無駄じゃなくて、むしろプラスに働いたんだろうか？
けどこいつは相変わらず皮肉ばっかり口にするし、全然弱くなったように見えない。
ううん、仮にこのサーヴァントがわたしに逆らって力が落ちても、わたしなんかじゃ十人いても太刀打ちできないんじゃないだろうか……？

pages.en:
“Um…”

…Then maybe that Command Spell wasn't wasted after all. Maybe it actually worked in my favor?

But he's still every bit as sarcastic as before, and he certainly doesn't look any weaker.

No—even if defying me did diminish his strength, I doubt ten of me together could stand against him…
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So…”
…That means the Command Spell wasn’t meaningless, and it worked in my favor?
But this guy speaks as sarcastically as always, and it doesn’t seem like he’s any weaker at all.
Though, even if he is weakened when going against me, I doubt even ten of me could take him on…

pages.ja:
「前言を撤回しよう、マスター。
年齢は若いが、君は卓越した魔術師だ。
子供と侮り、戦いから遠ざけようとしたのは私の過ちだった。無礼ともども謝ろう」
居を正して、礼儀正しく頭を下げる。
pages.jaRuby:

居を正して、礼儀正しく頭を下げる。
pages.en:
“I retract what I said, Master.

“Young though you are, you are an exceptional mage.

“I was wrong to dismiss you as a child and attempt to keep you from the fighting. I apologize for that, and for my discourtesy.”

He straightens his posture and bows with perfect formality.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Let me take back what I said before, Master.
You are young, but you are an outstanding magus.
It was my mistake to patronize you and try to keep you out of the battle. I apologize for my rudeness.”
He adjusts his stance and bows his head politely.

pages.ja:
「え
ちょっ、止めてよ、たしかに色々言い合ったけど、そんなのケンカ両成敗っていうか……」
「そうか。いや、話の解るマスターで助かった」
「……なんか、切り返し早いわねアンタ」
「なに、誤算は誤算だったが、嬉しい誤算というヤツだったからな。これほどの才能があるのなら、君を戦いに巻き込むことに異論はない」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Wha—hey, stop that. We both said plenty, so we were both at fault, or—well, let's just call it even…”

“Very well. I am fortunate to have a reasonable Master.”

“…You certainly change tack quickly.”
